html:
The Khanate of Khiva was an Uzbek state in Khwarazm, the irrigated plain of the lower Amu Darya south of the Aral Sea, from 1511 to 1920. It covered what is now western Uzbekistan and much of Turkmenistan. It was one of the Uzbek khanates, beside Bukhara and later Kokand.

Its first capital was Urgench, but around 1600, after the Amu Darya shifted its course, the court moved to Khiva. The Persian conqueror Nader Shah occupied the khanate from 1740 to 1746. From 1804 the Qongrat dynasty ruled.

Khiva lived from oasis farming and the caravan trade, and also from slave raiding: Turkmen raiders seized Persians and Russians and sold them in its market. Russia sent armies against Khiva in 1717 and 1839, and both failed in the desert. In 1873 a Russian army finally took the city, closed the slave market, and made the khan a Russian vassal.

In 1920 the Bolsheviks removed the last khan, and the land was later divided under Soviet rule. The walled inner town of Khiva, Itchan Kala, still stands.
